newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kidnappers free ex-Afghan provincial governor.
newsitem.headline: Kidnappers free ex-Afghan provincial governor.

text.p: A former Afghan provincial governor, Gul Agha, said on Monday he had been released by armed men who kidnapped him five days ago from the southwestern Pakistani town of Quetta.

Agha, former governor of the southern Afghan province of Kandahar, told reporters the Afghan kidnappers had released him on Sunday night. He said they were a group not connected with the Taleban Islamic movement.
Earlier, a member of Agha's family had blamed the kidnapping on the Taleban, who control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan including the capital, Kabul.
"The Taleban and their leadership were not involved in the kidnapping," Agha said.
He said he and his tribe knew who were responsible and added: "We will settle the issue with them according to tribal traditions."
Agha was kidnapped on Wednesday while supervising the construction of his house in Quetta, the capital of Baluchistan province bordering Afghanistan and Iran.
He was governor of Kandahar under ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani until the Taleban took control of the province in November 1994 in the early days of their drive for power.
Since then Agha has lived in Quetta as an exile.
